title: Glossa finding v1: one quality finding, from any layer (RFC 0005 §2.1)
description: The one shape a finding has, everywhere: in `glossa check`, in the Glossa pull-request check, in the server's stored check runs, in Studio and over MCP. A layer says what is wrong with which message in which locale; Context fills the locus's file, line, route, component, capture and region in at report time. Go: platform/internal/quality/domain.Finding.

fingerprint.description: Identifies the finding across re-runs and across surfaces. sha256 of the layer, the code, the message (its catalog ID where the caller has one, its key otherwise), the locale and the normalized subject — and of nothing else, so a reformatted file, a new source revision or a reworded explanation never re-opens a waiver.

layer.description: Which layer found it (RFC 0005 §3). Selectable by name in the policy and on the command line.

code.description: The rule. Stable, and shared with the CLI and the pull-request check; the MessageFormat kernel's codes keep their spelling (missing-argument, markup-renamed), as do Knowledge's (term_missing, term_forbidden).

severity.description: error or warning, plus waived — which is a rendering of a finding and not a third rank a layer may emit. A waived finding is still computed and still reported, counted on its own, and can never fail a check.

message.description: The explanation for a person. Its wording is not stable and it is deliberately not part of the fingerprint.

subject.description: What the finding names: the argument, the markup element, the term used. Part of the fingerprint, because two missing arguments in one message are two findings.

detail.description: Qualifies the code — the MessageFormat kernel's Detail, e.g. 'missing-fallback-variant' or 'number->string'.

evidence.description: What the layer measured. RFC 0005 §2.1 spells this `detail`; it is `evidence` here so the kernel's string `detail` — which every conversion before M4 dropped — keeps its own name and both survive. Free-form per code.

source_revision.description: The source revision the finding was computed against. A waiver dies when it changes (RFC 0005 §2.3).

waiver.description: The waiver that accepted this finding. Present exactly when severity is 'waived'.

allOf.description: A waived finding names its waiver, and only a waived finding does.

locus.description: Everything that locates a finding. Every field is optional and every field means the same thing in every layer.

message.description: The catalog message's ID. Absent where the caller has only the key, which is the case for an offline `glossa check`.

locale.description: The locale the finding is about (BCP 47); absent for a finding about the project rather than a translation.

revision.description: The translation revision the finding was computed against.

capture.description: The capture a visual finding is about.

span.description: The offending words in the source or the target, in bytes. It is what lets Studio and the overlay underline them instead of the whole string.

fix.description: A hint, never an action: nothing applies one without a person or an explicit --fix.

hint.description: The suggested text, where the layer can produce one.
